claim: Metabolism of host-targeted drugs by the microbiome can substantially impact host treatment success.
source: Metabolism of host-targeted drugs by the microbiome can substantially impact host treatment success.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that sets up the study's premise.

claim: Many host-targeted drugs inadvertently hamper microbiome growth.
source: since many host-targeted drugs inadvertently hamper microbiome growth, repeated drug administration can lead to microbiome evolutionary adaptation.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Most loss-of-function resistance mutations in Escherichia coli also reduced drug toxicity in the C. elegans host.
source: Genetic screens revealed that most of loss-of-function resistance mutations in Escherichia coli also reduced drug toxicity in the host.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic screens reported in the abstract.

claim: Resistance rapidly emerged in E. coli under natural selection.
source: We found that resistance rapidly emerged in E. coli under natural selection and converged to a handful of resistance mechanisms.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the evolution experiments reported in the abstract.

claim: Evolved resistance converged to a handful of resistance mechanisms.
source: We found that resistance rapidly emerged in E. coli under natural selection and converged to a handful of resistance mechanisms.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the evolution experiments reported in the abstract.

claim: Nutrient availability during bacterial evolution dictated the dietary effect on the host.
source: Surprisingly, we discovered that nutrient availability during bacterial evolution dictated the dietary effect on the host – only bacteria evolving in nutrient-poor media reduced host drug toxicity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study reported in the abstract.

claim: Only bacteria evolving in nutrient-poor media reduced host drug toxicity.
source: Surprisingly, we discovered that nutrient availability during bacterial evolution dictated the dietary effect on the host – only bacteria evolving in nutrient-poor media reduced host drug toxicity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study reported in the abstract.

claim: Bacterial metabolism substantially alters 65% of host-targeting drugs.
source: Recent systematic screens revealed that bacterial metabolism substantially alters 65% of host-targeting drugs (Lehouritis et al., 2015; Zimmermann et al., 2019) and in vivo studies demonstrated that bacterial metabolism has clinical implications in multiple cases (Spanogiannopoulos et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous systematic screens.

claim: Bacterial metabolism has clinical implications in multiple cases.
source: Recent systematic screens revealed that bacterial metabolism substantially alters 65% of host-targeting drugs (Lehouritis et al., 2015; Zimmermann et al., 2019) and in vivo studies demonstrated that bacterial metabolism has clinical implications in multiple cases (Spanogiannopoulos et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to in vivo studies.

claim: 25% of host-targeted drugs considerably hamper the growth of representative species of the gut microbiome at physiological concentrations.
source: A recent screen found that 25% of host-targeted drugs considerably hamper the growth of representative species of the gut microbiome at physiological concentrations (Maier et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a recent screen.

claim: Microbiome changes take place through shifts in species composition and fixation of beneficial mutations within individual species.
source: Microbiome changes take place through two fundamental processes: shifts in species composition (ecological changes) and fixation of beneficial mutations within individual species (intraspecies adaptation) (Garud et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Multiple metagenomic studies using 16S rRNA gene sequencing have repeatedly identified shifts in species composition in response to changes in host diet and drug treatment.
source: Multiple metagenomic studies using 16S rRNA gene sequencing have repeatedly identified shifts in species composition in response to changes in host diet and drug treatment (Forslund et al., 2015; Imhann et al., 2016; Jackson et al., 2018; Vich Vila et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to metagenomic studies.

claim: The gut environment rapidly selects for spontaneously arising beneficial mutations that can reach fixation within a few days.
source: Longitudinal studies in mouse models showed that the gut environment rapidly selects for spontaneously arising beneficial mutations that can reach fixation within a few days (Barroso-Batista et al., 2014; Crook et al., 2019; Lourenço et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to longitudinal studies in mouse models.

claim: C. elegans and its bacterial diet have been used as a model system for the discovery and mechanistic understanding of bacterial influences on the efficacy of drugs commonly prescribed to treat cancer and diabetes.
source: Specifically, C. elegans and its bacterial diet have been used as a model system for the discovery and mechanistic understanding of bacterial influences on the efficacy of drugs commonly prescribed to treat cancer and diabetes (García-González et al., 2017; Pryor et al., 2019b; Scott et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies using the C. elegans model system.

claim: 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and 5-fluoro-2'-deoxyuridine (FUDR) are antimetabolites used as chemotherapy.
source: The two closely related pro-drugs 5-ﬂuorouracil (5-FU) and 5-ﬂuoro-2'-deoxyuridine (FUDR) are two examples of such antimetabolites that are used as chemotherapy.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these drugs.

claim: The pro-drugs 5-FU and FUDR are transported into the cell and are sequentially modified into toxic compounds by the nucleotide synthesis network.
source: The pro-drugs, masquerading as extracellular nucleotides, are transported into the cell and are sequentially modified into toxic compounds by the nucleotide synthesis network.
evidence: This describes the known mechanism of action of these drugs.

claim: Intermediate compounds metabolized from fluoropyrimidines interfere with DNA and RNA synthesis in bacteria.
source: In bacteria, intermediate compounds metabolized from these fluoropyrimidines interfere with DNA and RNA synthesis, inhibit the synthesis of deoxythymidine monophosphate (Cohen et al., 1958), and lead to harmful accumulation of cell wall precursors (Tomasz and Borek, 1962; Tomasz and Borek, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Fluoropyrimidines inhibit the synthesis of deoxythymidine monophosphate in bacteria.
source: In bacteria, intermediate compounds metabolized from these fluoropyrimidines interfere with DNA and RNA synthesis, inhibit the synthesis of deoxythymidine monophosphate (Cohen et al., 1958), and lead to harmful accumulation of cell wall precursors (Tomasz and Borek, 1962; Tomasz and Borek, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cohen et al., 1958.

claim: Fluoropyrimidines lead to harmful accumulation of cell wall precursors in bacteria.
source: In bacteria, intermediate compounds metabolized from these fluoropyrimidines interfere with DNA and RNA synthesis, inhibit the synthesis of deoxythymidine monophosphate (Cohen et al., 1958), and lead to harmful accumulation of cell wall precursors (Tomasz and Borek, 1962; Tomasz and Borek, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tomasz and Borek, 1962 and 1960.

claim: Mutations in the bacterial gene network for nucleotide synthesis can both increase and decrease drug efficacy in the C. elegans host feeding on mutated bacteria.
source: Recent studies on these drugs revealed that mutations in the bacterial gene network for nucleotide synthesis can both increase and decrease drug efficacy in the C. elegans host feeding on mutated bacteria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to recent studies and Figure 1A.

claim: The main mechanism underlying the host effect is bacterial accumulation of the pro-drug intermediate 5-fluorouridine 5′-monophosphate (FUMP) that is highly cytotoxic for the animal.
source: The main mechanism underlying this host effect is bacterial accumulation of the pro-drug intermediate 5-fluorouridine 5′-monophosphate (FUMP) that is highly cytotoxic for the animal (García-González et al., 2017; Scott et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to García-González et al., 2017 and Scott et al., 2017.

claim: The IC50 for 5-FU in E. coli was 1.8 µM in nutrient-poor media and 35.5 µM in nutrient-rich media.
source: The IC50 for 5-FU was 1.8 µM and 35.5 µM in nutrient-poor and nutrient-rich media, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the Results section.

claim: The IC50 for FUDR in E. coli was 1.1 µM in nutrient-poor media and 5.5 µM in nutrient-rich media.
source: The IC50 for FUDR was 1.1 µM and 5.5 µM in nutrient-poor and nutrient-rich media, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the Results section.

claim: Bacteria growing on nutrient-poor media were significantly more sensitive to both 5-FU and FUDR than bacteria growing on nutrient-rich media.
source: bacteria growing on nutrient-poor media that lacks potentially competing metabolites were significantly more sensitive to both drugs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the IC50 measurements.

claim: The mean IC50 of 5-FU from 806 human cancer cell lines is 110 µM.
source: Interestingly, systematic measurements across 806 human cancer cell lines revealed a higher average inhibitory concentration of 110 µM 5-FU (Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2013.

claim: E. coli is more drug sensitive to 5-FU than many cell types tested from the human host.
source: Thus, E. coli is more drug sensitive than many cell types tested from the human host.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing E. coli IC50 values to human cancer cell line IC50 values.

claim: An average of 1.5 million independent barcodes were identified in each screen.
source: We identified an average of 1.5 million independent barcodes in each screen with an average coverage of about 500 reads for each unique barcode (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing experiments.

claim: Each individual barcode was identified on average 500 times.
source: We identified an average of 1.5 million independent barcodes in each screen with an average coverage of about 500 reads for each unique barcode (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing experiments.

claim: A perfect match to a known barcode was identified in 85% of sequenced reads.
source: We identified a perfect match to a known barcode in 85% of sequenced reads.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing analysis.

claim: Biological duplicates showed very high correlation (Pearson r > 0.93) in barcode frequency.
source: Reassuringly, we observed a very high correlation (Pearson r > 0.93) when we compared the frequency of barcodes in biological duplicates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the experimental replicates.

claim: Most gene-knockouts in the core pathways for nucleotide salvage and drug activation increased drug resistance.
source: Overall, most gene-knockouts in the core pathways for nucleotide salvage and drug activation increased drug resistance.
evidence: This is a summary of the screen results for the nucleotide synthesis network.

claim: Gene-knockouts in the pathway for de-novo nucleotide synthesis increased drug susceptibility.
source: In contrast, gene-knockouts in the pathway for de-novo nucleotide synthesis increased drug susceptibility.
evidence: This is a summary of the screen results for the nucleotide synthesis network.

claim: Knockout of either udp or tdk conferred resistance only in nutrient-rich media for both drugs.
source: For example, knockout of either udp or tdk conferred resistance only in nutrient-rich media (for both drugs) while knockout of upp or uraA conferred resistance only in nutrient-poor media.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the screen results.

claim: Knockout of upp or uraA conferred resistance only in nutrient-poor media.
source: For example, knockout of either udp or tdk conferred resistance only in nutrient-rich media (for both drugs) while knockout of upp or uraA conferred resistance only in nutrient-poor media.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the screen results.

claim: Strains mutated in the de-novo synthesis pathway were completely missing from all nutrient-poor screens, including the control experiment.
source: Additionally, we observed that strains mutated in the de-novo synthesis pathway were completely missing from all nutrient-poor screens, including the control experiment.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the screen results.

claim: The absence of strains mutated in the de-novo synthesis pathway from nutrient-poor screens reflects the essential role of de-novo nucleotide synthesis if nucleotides are not supplemented in the media.
source: This absence reflects the essential role of de-novo nucleotide synthesis if nucleotides are not supplemented in the media.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the screen results based on biological knowledge.

claim: Strains mutated in the de-novo synthesis pathway were under-represented relative to the control experiment in nutrient-rich media.
source: In nutrient-rich media, strains mutated in the de-novo synthesis pathway were detected but were under-represented relative to the control experiment.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the screen results.

claim: Knockout of the de-novo nucleotide synthesis pathway increases bacterial drug sensitivity in nutrient-rich conditions.
source: This observation indicates that knockout of the de-novo nucleotide synthesis pathway increases bacterial drug sensitivity in nutrient-rich conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the screen results.

claim: Considerably more knockout strains emerged as resistant in nutrient-rich media (49–50) relative to nutrient-poor media (12–24) for both drugs.
source: Second, in both drugs considerably more knockout strains emerged as resistant in nutrient-rich media (49–50) relative to nutrient-poor media (12–24).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the screen results.

claim: The precision of the genetic screen was estimated to be around 80%.
source: We estimated that the precision of the genetic screen was around 80% by testing an individual subset of hit strains in 69 growth experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a validation measurement of the screen methodology.

claim: Across 16 sequenced genomes, 75 mutations affecting 49 genes were identified, with 80% of them within coding sequences.
source: Across 16 sequenced genomes we identified 75 mutations affecting 49 genes, 80% of them within coding sequences.
evidence: This is a summary of the whole genome sequencing results.

claim: At least 55% of all mutations lead to gene loss-of-function.
source: We predicted that at least 55% of all mutations lead to gene loss-of-function (large deletions, transposon insertions, and premature stop codons).
evidence: This is an analysis of the mutation types identified in the sequencing.

claim: Only 11 genes out of the 89 resistance hits are affiliated with the known target pathway (the gene network of nucleotide synthesis).
source: Interestingly, only 11 genes out of the 89 resistance hits are affiliated with the known target pathway (the gene network of nucleotide synthesis).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the screen hits.

claim: 60 out of 89 hit genes can be assigned to just eight enriched pathways.
source: Inspection of the annotated functions of the 89 hit genes we previously identified with DESeq2 revealed that 60 of them can be assigned to just to eight enriched pathways (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a functional analysis of the screen hits.

claim: Six of the eight enriched pathways are metabolically linked through the pentose phosphate pathway which synthesizes ribulose-5-phosphate (RU5P), a precursor for nucleotide synthesis.
source: Interestingly, six of these pathways are metabolically linked through the pentose phosphate pathway which synthesizes ribulose-5-phosphate (RU5P), a precursor for nucleotide synthesis.
evidence: This is an analysis of the metabolic connections between the enriched pathways.

claim: 43 out of the 69 strains identified as 5-FU resistant were tested previously as C. elegans diet.
source: Forty-three out of the 69 strains we identified as 5-FU resistant were tested previously as C. elegans diet.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study and a previous study.

claim: Only 12% of 3814 tested bacterial strains considerably increased 5-FU resistance in the C. elegans host (>10-fold).
source: the C. elegans screen revealed that only 12% of 3814 tested bacterial strains considerably increased 5-FU resistance in the host (>10-fold)
evidence: This is a summary of results from a previous C. elegans screen.

claim: 40% of the 43 bacterial resistance hits considerably increased 5-FU resistance in the C. elegans host.
source: however, this proportion increased to 40% in the subset of 43 hits that confer 5-FU bacterial resistance.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study's hits and previous C. elegans screen results.

claim: 59% of gene knockouts that substantially increase bacterial resistance and do not hamper bacterial growth increased 5-FU resistance in the C. elegans host.
source: Moreover, when the gene knockouts were restricted only to those that substantially increase bacterial resistance and that do not hamper bacterial growth, this proportion increased to 59% (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a refined analysis of the overlap between bacterial resistance and host effects.

claim: All evolved strains had increased drug resistance.
source: As the figure shows, all evolved strains had increased drug resistance.
evidence: This is a summary of the evolution experiment results.

claim: Increases in IC50 ranged from about twofold for adaptation to 5-FU in nutrient-rich media to more than 60-fold for FUDR adaptation in nutrient-poor media.
source: Increases in IC50 ranged from about twofold, for adaptation to 5-FU in nutrient-rich media, to more than 60-fold for FUDR adaptation in nutrient-poor media.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the resistance levels achieved in the evolution experiments.

claim: Strains evolved in a specific media and one drug become resistant to both drugs in that media.
source: Strains evolved in a specific media and one drug become resistant to both drugs in that media.
evidence: This is a summary of the cross-resistance analysis.

claim: In most cases, strains were not resistant to the same drug they evolved on if it was combined with the other media type.
source: In most cases, the strains were not resistant to the same drug they evolved on if it was combined with the other media type (strains that evolved in nutrient-poor media with FUDR where the only exception).
evidence: This is a summary of the cross-resistance analysis.

claim: 4 of the 12 tested evolved clones from 5-FU evolution considerably lowered 5-FU toxicity in C. elegans.
source: As the figure shows, 4 of the 12 tested evolved clones considerably lowered 5-FU toxicity in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for 5-FU evolved strains.

claim: Only bacterial clones that evolved in nutrient-poor media with 5-FU had an impact on the C. elegans host (four of four independently evolved clones).
source: Surprisingly, this pattern perfectly coincides with the nutritional history of our evolved clones: only bacterial clones that evolved in nutrient-poor media had an impact on the host (four of four independently evolved clones).
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for 5-FU evolved strains.

claim: Bacterial clones evolved on 5-FU in nutrient-rich media had no impact on drug-toxicity in C. elegans (eight of eight tested clones, including four of four independently evolved clones).
source: Although bacterial clones evolved on 5-FU in nutrient-rich media also became drug resistant, their resistance mechanism had no impact on drug-toxicity in C. elegans (eight of eight tested clones), including four of four independently evolved clones.
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for 5-FU evolved strains.

claim: 9 of the 18 evolved clones from FUDR evolution considerably lowered FUDR toxicity in C. elegans.
source: As the figure shows, 9 of the 18 evolved clones considerably lowered FUDR toxicity in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for FUDR evolved strains.

claim: Only bacterial clones that evolved in nutrient-poor media with FUDR had an impact on the C. elegans host (nine of nine tested clones).
source: Again, this pattern perfectly coincides with nutritional history of evolved strains: only bacterial clones that evolved in nutrient-poor media had an impact on host (nine of nine tested clones)
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for FUDR evolved strains.

claim: Bacterial clones evolved on FUDR in nutrient-rich media had no impact on the host (nine of nine tested clones, including four of four independently evolved clones).
source: while clones evolving on FUDR in nutrient-rich media had no impact on the host (nine of nine tested clones), including four of four independently evolved clones.
evidence: This is a summary of the C. elegans drug sensitivity experiments for FUDR evolved strains.

claim: The association between nutrient availability during evolution and host effect is statistically significant (p=0.00016).
source: In order to test if this perfect match between nutrient availability and host effect is statistically significant given the 16 independently evolved clones from both 5-FU and FUDR conditions, we used a two-tailed Fisher exact test (using evolution history and host effect as categories). The test rejected the hypothesis that nutrient availability during evolution is randomly associated with the host effect (p=0.00016).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the relationship between nutrient availability and host effect.

claim: In nutrient-poor media, upp was frequently inactivated (six of eight evolved strains).
source: Specifically, in nutrient-poor media we observed that upp, a gene central for nucleotide salvage, was frequently inactivated (six of eight).
evidence: This is a summary of the mutation patterns from whole genome sequencing.

claim: In nutrient-poor media, pyrE was frequently modified (three of eight evolved strains).
source: Additionally, we observed that pyrE, an essential gene for pyrimidine de-novo synthesis, was frequently modified (three of eight).
evidence: This is a summary of the mutation patterns from whole genome sequencing.

claim: In nutrient-rich media, evolved resistance frequently (four of eight) selected for modification of the pyrH gene.
source: In contrast, evolved resistance in nutrient-rich media frequently (four of eight) selected for modification of the pyrH gene, a UMP kinase involved in drug activation and a regulator of de-novo nucleotide synthesis (Kholti et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a summary of the mutation patterns from whole genome sequencing.

claim: pyrH is a UMP kinase involved in drug activation and a regulator of de-novo nucleotide synthesis.
source: In contrast, evolved resistance in nutrient-rich media frequently (four of eight) selected for modification of the pyrH gene, a UMP kinase involved in drug activation and a regulator of de-novo nucleotide synthesis (Kholti et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a functional description of pyrH supported by citation.

claim: In nutrient-rich conditions, fimE was frequently (six of eight) inactivated.
source: In nutrient-rich conditions, we also observed frequent (six of eight) inactivation of fimE, a regulator of fimA involved in cell adhesion.
evidence: This is a summary of the mutation patterns from whole genome sequencing.

claim: tdk was frequently (four of eight) inactivated in FUDR-, but not 5-FU-, evolved strains.
source: Only one gene was characterized by a drug-specific pattern – tdk coding for kinase of deoxythymidine and deoxyuridine was frequently (four of eight) inactivated in FUDR-, but not 5-FU-, evolved strains.
evidence: This is a summary of the mutation patterns from whole genome sequencing.

claim: Nutrient-rich media evolved strains showed a significantly higher number of differentially expressed genes relative to the strains that evolved on nutrient-poor media.
source: This analysis revealed that an extensive transcriptional reprogramming, involving hundreds of genes, took place in nutrient-rich media evolved strains. In contrast, strains that evolved on nutrient-poor media underwent a modest reprogramming that involved only a few dozens of genes.
evidence: This is a summary of the RNA-seq analysis results.

claim: All evolved strains overexpressed the pathway for de-novo nucleotide synthesis.
source: As the figure shows, we observed that the transcriptional changes in the target gene network agreed with our interpretation of the mutational pattern and aligned with expectations from the genetic screen: all evolved strains overexpressed the pathway for de-novo nucleotide synthesis and overall inhibit the pathway for nucleotide salvage and pro-drug activation, albeit through different genes.
evidence: This is a summary of the RNA-seq analysis for the nucleotide synthesis network.

claim: All evolved strains overall inhibit the pathway for nucleotide salvage and pro-drug activation, albeit through different genes.
source: As the figure shows, we observed that the transcriptional changes in the target gene network agreed with our interpretation of the mutational pattern and aligned with expectations from the genetic screen: all evolved strains overexpressed the pathway for de-novo nucleotide synthesis and overall inhibit the pathway for nucleotide salvage and pro-drug activation, albeit through different genes.
evidence: This is a summary of the RNA-seq analysis for the nucleotide synthesis network.

claim: Poor media evolved strains reduced nucleotide salvage through upp knockout.
source: Poor media evolved strains reduced nucleotide salvage through upp knockout while nutrient-rich media evolved strains repressed udp expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the mechanisms by which different evolved strains reduced nucleotide salvage.

claim: Nutrient-rich media evolved strains repressed udp expression.
source: Poor media evolved strains reduced nucleotide salvage through upp knockout while nutrient-rich media evolved strains repressed udp expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the mechanisms by which different evolved strains reduced nucleotide salvage.

claim: Nutrient-rich media evolved strains also inhibited the expression of two additional kinases (ndk and cmk) involved in drug phosphorylation.
source: Lastly, nutrient-rich media evolved strains also inhibited the expression of two additional kinases (ndk and cmk) involved in drug phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a summary of the RNA-seq analysis results.

claim: Central carbon metabolism was repressed in all evolved strains.
source: For example, central carbon metabolism was repressed in all strains (see oxidative phosphorylation and citrate cycle).
evidence: This is a summary of the pathway enrichment analysis from RNA-seq.

claim: Rich media evolved strains repressed multiple additional potentially relevant pathways, such as lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis and phenylalanine metabolism.
source: Additionally, rich media evolved strains repressed multiple additional potentially relevant pathways identified in our screen, such as lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis and phenylalanine metabolism.
evidence: This is a summary of the pathway enrichment analysis from RNA-seq.

claim: Nutrient-poor media evolved strains induced the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway.
source: Interestingly, nutrient-poor media evolved strains induced the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway, potentially increasing flux into the pentose phosphate pathway.
evidence: This is a summary of the pathway enrichment analysis from RNA-seq with an interpretation.

claim: The repression of flagellar assembly, observed in all evolved strains, may increase drug resistance by inactivation of a highly demanding cellular process that is unneeded in a serial transfer experiment.
source: For example, the repression of flagellar assembly, observed in all evolved strains, may increase drug resistance by inactivation of a highly demanding cellular process that is unneeded in a serial transfer experiment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNA-seq results.

claim: Inactivation of the regulator fimE leads cells to shift their lifestyle from planktonic to pellicle-like growth in broth cultures without reducing the growth rate.
source: Previous work revealed that inactivation of the regulator fimE leads cells to shift their lifestyle from planktonic to pellicle-like growth in broth cultures without reducing the growth rate (Matange et al., 2019; Stentebjerg-Olesen et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Pellicle formation by fimE inactivation was observed to be selected for in E. coli cells exposed to the antibiotic rifamycin and was found to improve resistance by increasing cell aggregation due to increased cell adhesion.
source: Pellicle formation by fimE inactivation was also observed to be selected for in E. coli cells exposed to the antibiotic rifamycin and was found to improve resistance by increasing cell aggregation due to increased cell adhesion (Matange et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The E. coli barcoded deletion library has 3680 individual knockout strains.
source: The strain collection has 3680 individual knockout strains.
evidence: This is a description of the strain collection used in the study.

claim: In the barcoded library, the open reading frame of a single gene was replaced in-frame with a fragment containing turbo GFP, chloramphenicol resistance cassette, and a unique 20 bp sequence that serves as an identification barcode.
source: In each strain the open reading frame of a single gene was replaced in-frame with a fragment containing turbo GFP, chloramphenicol resistance cassette, and a unique 20 bp sequence that serves as an identification barcode.
evidence: This is a description of the construction of the strain collection.

claim: The parent strain of the barcoded library is BW38028 with the genotype Δ(araD-araB)567 lacZp-4105(UV5)-lacY λ- hsdR514, rph+.
source: The parent strain of this library is BW38028 with the genotype Δ(araD-araB)567 lacZp-4105(UV5)-lacY λ- hsdR514, rph+ (Conway et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the parent strain with citation.

claim: The N2 (Bristol) C. elegans strain was used in the study.
source: We used the N2 (Bristol) C. elegans strain.
evidence: This is a description of the C. elegans strain used.
